editorial.headline: Wholesale Building Materials: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This wholesale construction-materials activity permits 100% foreign ownership nationally, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks its PMA registration on the island.
editorial.body:
A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today, despite its national foreign-investment opening. The activity itself is the wholesale trade of construction materials made from clay, lime, cement or glass. Its defined range includes pressed and kodok-style roof tiles; pressed, hollow and refractory bricks; floor and wall tiles; concrete tiles; air vents; baths and toilets; eternit cement sheets; irrigation pipes; and buis drainage pipes. The common thread is wholesale distribution of these specified building products through the construction-materials supply chain.

The record opens registration to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar businesses. That breadth is significant: this is not presented as an activity reserved for one stated enterprise size. A micro or small business may sit within the same classification, as may a medium or large enterprise. For founders, the scale field gives a clear national registration perimeter, but it does not settle the separate question of where PMA registration remains possible.

Nationally, the PMA setting is TERBUKA and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. In plain terms, the activity may be wholly foreign-owned under the national position recorded here; no lower national ownership ceiling is shown. That position is sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. It is a real national permission, but it should not be mistaken for a guarantee of identical registration treatment in Bali, where the relevant restriction operates through a provincial risk-based rule.

Bali is therefore the decisive qualification. Its status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO, and the record states that the activity is blocked by the Bali moratorium. At the Besar scale, OSS assigns Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk across every scope of the activity. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for KBLI activities in those Low and Medium-Low risk bands, with the record identifying the restriction from May 2026. The practical conclusion is exact: national openness does not override the Bali restriction, so PMA registration for this activity cannot be made there today.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not override Bali’s permanent PMA restriction for the risk bands assigned to this activity.
